label: r4c2
name: Mirrored head, 1 epoch, 64 minibatches
hypothesis: Same network as r3c1, with 1 PPO epoch (about 400k samples) and 64 minibatches of 64 samples each. That doubles the gradient steps per update, which offsets the loss of the second epoch while every sample is still seen only once. Fresh data and more optimiser steps should together beat r3c1. Refuted if mean dev success is at or below 0.90, or clearly below the plain 1-epoch candidate.
last_analysis: Every trial without the x-mirrored footprint head collapsed to an immediate DONE and scored 0. With the mirror, the task is learnable. The biggest gain so far came from more samples: dropping from 4 PPO epochs to 2 roughly doubled the samples and moved dev success from 0.65 to 0.90 (seeds 0.94 and 0.86), well beyond the ~0.2 seed spread. A longer credit horizon (0.62), landing-layer attention (0.59), a deeper dilated net (0.35) and the orientation-agnostic head (0.48) all scored at or below the mirrored baseline. r3c1's training success levelled off near 0.87 from 75% of training onward, and its dev IoU is 0.99, so the remaining failures are small ordering or completion errors. For the last round I keep the r3c1 network. I test 1 PPO epoch (about 400k samples), 1 epoch with smaller minibatches (more gradient steps), and a wider trunk at 1 epoch, which keeps about r3c1's sample count and tests whether capacity is the limit.
